cohort: Neonates admitted to selected hospitals in the Gurage zone, Ethiopia, from June 2019 to June 2021
finding: The prevalence of RDS in the study area was high (45.1%), and several factors were associated with increased odds of RDS, including preterm birth, jaundice, sepsis, cesarean delivery, and young or advanced maternal age.
mod_finding: The odds of RDS in neonates born via Caesarean section were 1.7 times higher compared with those delivered via spontaneous and instrumental delivery.
